about: The questions the incident team would put to bodies and experts who could give an official view on Storm Charles, by field. Drafts: none has been sent; a person sends every message. No contact details are kept. Generated from outreach/README.md.

questions.question: At what times (UTC) were Lisbon's red warnings for wind and for rain issued? The open data gives the period each covers, not when it was issued.
questions.what_we_have_now: the lead-time table, now part press, part two reads.

questions.question: Was the track ("between Sines and Cabo Carvoeiro") the main uncertainty on Tuesday, and when did the models agree?
questions.what_we_have_now: why the rain warning went red about nine hours after the wind.

questions.question: The government's statement cites a possible sting jet with gusts above 150 km/h. What probability did IPMA attach to it, and was it observed?
questions.what_we_have_now: quoted via the government; our analysis only.

questions.question: The airport forecast (TAF) weakened at 23:00 on Tuesday while the red warnings stood. How should the public read a point forecast for pilots against a district warning?
How does Charles compare with Kristin, in measured gusts and rainfall, once the stations are in?
Who named the storm, on what date, and under which criterion?
For independent scientists: is there anything in our analysis that is wrong or overstated?
When was the decision taken to recommend that large events be suspended on Wednesday, and on what criteria (the warning level, the tide, the wind on structures)?
Is there a written threshold at which an indoor event with outdoor structures and tens of thousands of people is advised to close, or is it case by case?
How many incidents were recorded in the Lisbon district between Tuesday 00:00 and Thursday 00:00, by type?
Which public warning channels were used (cell broadcast, SMS, the site), in which languages, and at what times? Did visitors on foreign SIM cards receive them?
What would you want an aggregator like this site to do, and not do, during an alert?
At what time was the recommendation to suspend Web Summit on Wednesday communicated to the organisers, and in what form?
questions.what_we_have_now: press at 17:53; the organisers' page says the government "formally advised".

questions.question: Does an "alert situation" oblige the suspension of an event in a private venue, or only recommend it? Who decides?

questions.audience: Metro, Carris, CP, Fertagus, Transtejo Soflusa, Lusoponte, IP, ANA, NAV
questions.question: What service ran on Wednesday between 12:00 and 21:00, and what was suspended, at what times?

questions.audience: Metro, Carris, CP, Fertagus, Transtejo Soflusa, Lusoponte, IP, ANA, NAV
questions.question: What wind or water thresholds close a line, a bridge, a ferry crossing or a runway, and are they published?

questions.audience: Metro, Carris, CP, Fertagus, Transtejo Soflusa, Lusoponte, IP, ANA, NAV
questions.question: When was Thursday morning's service confirmed, and through which channel first?

questions.audience: Metro, Carris, CP, Fertagus, Transtejo Soflusa, Lusoponte, IP, ANA, NAV
questions.question: For the airport: how many flights were cancelled or diverted on Wednesday, and when did operations return to normal?
At what time did the organisers decide, and what was the last piece of information that settled it?
questions.what_we_have_now: the page was published 19:09; press reported the government's recommendation at 17:53.

questions.question: What happens to Wednesday's programme (talks, the PITCH semi-final, Night Summit, side events), and to Wednesday-only tickets?
questions.what_we_have_now: unannounced; PITCH timing in conflict between two sources.

questions.question: Through which channels, in what order, was the decision communicated (email, app, the website, social)? We read the page at its source 109 minutes after it was published: it sat outside the paths our watch read.
For the venues: what is the rated wind limit of the temporary structures between the halls, and what caused the water ingress reported on Tuesday afternoon?
For practitioners: for an event of this size, what lead time is normal between a red warning and a decision to close a day, and what does good practice say about announcing it?
Is your article's time and by-line right in our list? (Copied from each page's own metadata.)
What did you want to confirm and could not, for lack of a primary source? (That list is our research list too.)
Would a single public timeline of decisions, each with its primary source and time, have been useful on Tuesday evening, and in what form?
